## Diverging Signals
- **Fear gauges say calmer, price and rates say stressed.** VIX is 17.33 and VVIX fell 9.15% to 97.15. But NDX is 6.0% under its high, the 10Y is 5.117%, Brent is $109.41 and HY OAS is through 3.25%. Implication: the market is not panicking, but the cause of the Oct 14–16 damage (rates and oil) has not gone away. A calm VIX with high yields is the setup that breaks when yields push higher.
- **Small caps and the Dow led, tech lagged.** Russell +1.65% and DJI +1.02% against NDX −0.13%. That is healthier breadth than Monday, but TQQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, so it did not share in it.
- **VXN is still high while VIX is low.** VXN 25.22 against VIX 17.33. Nasdaq-100 options are priced for much bigger swings than the S&P 500, which is the tension for TQQQ in particular.
- **The 10Y neutralizer leg is almost met (1.7bp away) while Brent is not (−8.6% away).** Rates are easing before oil is.

## TQQQ Read
- **Momentum:** RSI(14) is 35.9, neutral. It was 37.5 last read, so it slipped 1.6 points, and it is 5.9 points above oversold (below 30). For a put seller, a reading near oversold usually keeps premium (the price paid for the option) fairly rich. But there is no confirmed turn: the bounce was one day and the next day was red.
- **Market structure:** SIDEWAYS. Spot is 17.5% below the 4-week high ($85.32), short of the "more than 20% below" test (the line is $68.26, 3.0% under spot). Spot is 4.4% above the 4-week low ($67.43), far from the 30% needed for RALLY (about $87.66). The VXN leg of DOWNTURN is met (25.22 ≥ 25), but the price leg is not. One more red day of about 3% would flip this to DOWNTURN.
- **Trend:** Mixed to weak. Spot is 5.36% under the 50DMA ($74.40) and about 8.7% above the 200DMA. It is 19.73% under the 52-week high. The cushion above the 200DMA narrowed from about 9.2% to 8.7%.
- **Volatility & premium environment:** VXN is 25.22. The 3x-VXN estimate gives about 76% IV (an estimate, not a quote), and it probably runs hot. The option chain was not available this run, so TQQQ ATM IV, IV/HV (options cost versus actual recent movement) and put/call are all unknown. SKEW (160.40) says downside protection is still expensive. VVIX (97.15) says volatility itself is steadier than a day ago. TQQQ moves about 3 times the Nasdaq-100, so swings stay large.
- **Put-selling context: CAUTIOUS.** VIX at 17.33 and falling VVIX are friendlier than last read, and VXN at 25 means premium is likely still rich. But NDX is under 30,000, TQQQ is under its 50DMA, high-yield credit is still through its warning line, and the 10Y and Brent both sit near the levels that hurt on Oct 14–16. Premium richness cannot be confirmed from the chain today. The FOMC decision on Oct 28 is inside the 5-session window.
